title: Ephemeral probe capture & rollback harness for fast canary failover
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
We see recurring autoscaler thrash and cross-region failover incidents triggered by transient probe anomalies during canary deploys and cold-start windows. This ticket implements an ephemeral probe-capture and rollback harness (EPCRH) that buffers short-lived probe failures from influencing the autoscaler or triggering circuit breakers, and provides a fast automated rollback path for canary rollouts that show sustained degradation. The goal is to preserve user-facing SLOs during rapid deploys and region failovers without masking real regressions.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Current readiness/liveness probes feed directly into the health federation and autoscaler inputs. Short bursts (10s–2m) of probe noise during canary boot or kernel warmup cause aggressive eviction and regional handoff, breaching tail latency SLOs.
- Manual intervention and slow rollbacks lead to extended SLO breaches.
- We need a deterministic, observable mechanism that: (1) distinguishes ephemeral probe anomalies from sustained degradations, (2) prevents autoscaler thrash and unnecessary multi-region failovers, and (3) enables an automated-but-reversible rollback when canary signals persist.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Ephemeral Probe Capture (EPC): capture probe failures and successful heartbeats in a short-lived ring buffer (configurable window: default 90s) attached to each instance. The EPC emits a summarized signal to the health mediator rather than raw pass/fail ticks.
2) Probe Sanitizer Rules: apply a two-tier filter before feeding the autoscaler and circuit-breaker inputs: a) spike suppression (n-of-m threshold) to ignore short bursts, b) trend detector (exponential moving average + slope) to detect sustained degradation.
3) Rollback Harness: when trend detector exceeds sustained-failure threshold for a canary cohort, create an automated rollback action with a non-destructive preflight (snapshot of traffic split, metrics snapshot). The rollback action is gated by an approval policy that can be automated for low-risk changes and manual for high-risk releases.
4) Autoscaler integration: autoscaler will use sanitized health signals and a derated admission policy during canaries (lower take rate for unhealthy instances while preventing mass evictions).
5) Observability & Audit: expose EPC buffer traces in Console (per-instance trace) and add a canary incident dashboard (error budget burn, sanitized health curve, rollback decisions). Log all rollback and gating decisions to audit logs.

Trade-offs considered:
- Window length: longer windows reduce false positives but delay detection of real regressions. Default 90s chosen as compromise; configurable per-service.
- Local buffer vs centralized aggregator: local buffer avoids increased probe fan-out and latency; central aggregation would simplify cross-instance correlation but add complexity. We chose local EPC with periodic summarization.
- Automatic rollback aggressiveness: too aggressive -> rollbacks for flakey infra; too lax -> delays in mitigation. We provide policy templates and conservative defaults.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- No autoscaler thrash incidents attributable to canary probe noise in 30 days after rollout (baseline measured in last 30d).
- Canary rollbacks triggered by EPCRH match manual rollback decisions in >=90% of simulated regressions in staging exercises.
- End-to-end median P99 latency across regions does not increase; overall SLO incident rate decreases by at least 30% for deploy-time regressions.
- Console exposes per-canary sanitized health curve and EPC trace within 2 minutes of event.

Work items (implementation plan):
- RFC & design doc (confluence): architecture diagram, config knobs, failure modes (owner: Jonas) [link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/EPCRH-2026].
- Runtime changes: add per-instance EPC buffer, summarizer hook, probe sanitizer pipeline (owner: runtime infra).
- Autoscaler changes: accept sanitized signals + add canary derating policy (owner: scaling team).
- Console: new dashboard and per-instance EPC trace UI (owner: console team).
- Rollout policy: policy templates, canary cohorts, and approval flows (owner: platform PM).
- E2E tests: chaos testing for transient network blips and staged regressions, integration tests for rollback path (owner: SRE).

Observability and instrumentation:
- New metrics: epc_buffer_size, epc_filtered_spikes, epc_trend_score, canary_rollback_reason, sanitized_health_rate.
- Trace logs: epc_snapshot_id, probe_event_ids.
- Dashboards: canary incident summary, per-region SLO burn correlated with sanitized health scores.

Rollout plan / safety steps:
1) Deploy EPC as opt-in flag for a single non-critical service in staging.
2) Run 2 weeks of synthetic warm-up + chaos tests.
3) Roll to low-traffic production service with telemetry-only mode (no effect on autoscaler).
4) Enable sanitized signals for autoscaler for a small percentage of deploys (10%) and monitor.
5) Ramp to full enable after 7 days of stable metrics.

Testing & simulation:
- Use the probe-sim harness (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/probe-sim) to create spike/noise patterns and sustained degradation scenarios.
- Simulate multi-region failover combined with canary rollout to ensure EPCRH prevents unnecessary region handoffs.

Documentation & runbook:
- Add runbook for SREs describing how to inspect EPC traces, force rollback, and tune thresholds.
- Provide policy templates for product teams to choose conservative or aggressive rollback behavior.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should EPC buffers be persisted across short-lived restarts to avoid losing context? (initially no; evaluate after pilot).
- Best default thresholds for memory-constrained instances.

Related artifacts / links:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/EPCRH-2026
- Probe sim repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probe-sim
- Draft PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123
- Dashboard mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/EPCRH-mockups

Acceptance criteria checklist (short):
- [ ] EPC implemented with configurable window
- [ ] Probe sanitizer rules prototype in staging
- [ ] Autoscaler accepts sanitized signals behind a flag
- [ ] Console shows EPC traces and canary rollback events
- [ ] E2E chaos tests pass for transient spikes
- [ ] Runbook and policy templates published
comments: 2026-02-22 — Carlos Mendoza (SRE): Reviewed design; requested explicit failure-mode where EPC itself becomes saturated. Suggested backpressure metric and a hard cap metric emitted to health mediator.
2026-02-25 — Priya Rao (PM): Added product constraints — rollback automation should be opt-in per release stream. Also requested canary cohort size default set to 5% of traffic.

2026-03-01 — Jonas Meyer (ENG): Implemented EPC buffer prototype in runtime branch. Added local summarizer and exposed epc_trend_score metric. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123
2026-03-05 — Dalia Nguyen (QA): Started integration tests in staging. Early finding: 30s short spikes still occasionally pass sanitizer; increased spike suppression threshold recommended.
2026-03-10 — Aisha Patel (Owner): Enabled telemetry-only mode for two low-traffic services in prod. Monitoring dashboards linked and will observe for 7 days before enabling autoscaler integration.
